breakfast.name: Rohlik s Máslem (Bread Roll with Butter)
instructions: Split rohlíky
Spread with butter
Layer ham and cheese
Add tomato and cucumber slices
Eat with coffee
breakfast.description: The everyday Czech breakfast — crescent rolls from the bakery with butter, ham, and cheese. Simple, fast, and always good.

breakfast.name: Lívance (Czech Pancakes)
instructions: Mix flour, milk, eggs, sugar, yeast, salt
Let batter rise 20 min
Fry small thick pancakes in butter until golden on both sides
Stack on plate
Top with plum jam and sour cream
breakfast.description: Small, thick yeast pancakes — softer and puffier than Western pancakes. Served with plum jam and sour cream.

breakfast.name: Sázené Vejce s Uzeninou (Baked Eggs with Smoked Meat)
instructions: Fry sliced smoked meat in butter
Crack eggs over the meat
Cook until eggs are set
Serve in the pan with bread for dipping
breakfast.description: Eggs fried over smoked meat — a hearty Czech breakfast, especially on weekends.

lunch.name: Svíčková na Smetaně (Marinated Beef in Cream Sauce)
instructions: Lard beef, marinate overnight with sliced vegetables, vinegar, and spices
Brown beef on all sides in butter
Add vegetables, roast until browned
Add marinade and water, braise covered 2-2.5 hours until tender
Remove beef, blend sauce with vegetables until smooth
Strain, add cream, adjust with lemon juice and sugar
Slice beef, pour cream sauce over
Serve with bread dumplings and cranberry sauce
lunch.description: The Czech national dish — beef braised then served in a tangy cream-vegetable sauce with bread dumplings and cranberries.

lunch.name: Vepřo-knedlo-zelo (Pork, Dumplings, Sauerkraut)
instructions: Season pork with caraway, garlic, salt
Roast at 180°C for 90 min, basting frequently
Make sauerkraut: simmer with onion, caraway, pinch of sugar
Slice pork
Serve with bread dumplings and sauerkraut
lunch.description: The holy Czech trinity — roast pork with crackling, bread dumplings, and sauerkraut.

lunch.name: Kulajda (Creamy Mushroom-Dill Soup)
instructions: Sauté mushrooms in butter
Add diced potatoes and water, simmer until potatoes are tender
Add cream, bring back to simmer
Add generous chopped dill
Season with vinegar, salt, pepper
Poach an egg for each serving
Ladle soup into bowls with a poached egg on top
lunch.description: Creamy mushroom and dill soup from South Bohemia — the dill and vinegar tang sets it apart from any other mushroom soup.

dinner.name: Smažený Sýr (Fried Cheese)
instructions: Coat cheese: flour, egg, breadcrumbs, egg again, breadcrumbs again (double-coat)
Fry in hot oil until golden on both sides
Serve immediately with tartar sauce and potatoes or fries
dinner.description: Deep-fried cheese — a Czech institution found on every pub menu. The double breading keeps the cheese from escaping.

dinner.name: Guláš (Czech Goulash)
instructions: Brown beef in batches
Slowly cook onions until deeply golden — 15 min, essential
Add paprika off heat, stir
Add tomato paste, garlic, caraway, marjoram
Add water to cover, simmer low 2 hours until beef falls apart
Sauce should be thick from dissolved onions, not flour
Serve over bread dumplings
dinner.description: Czech guláš — thicker than Hungarian gulyás, more onion and caraway, always served over bread dumplings.

dinner.name: Pečená Kachna (Roast Duck)
instructions: Season duck with caraway, marjoram, salt
Prick skin all over to render fat
Roast at 160°C for 2 hours, basting with rendered fat
Raise heat to 200°C for final 20 min to crisp skin
Rest 15 min, carve
Serve with braised cabbage and dumplings
dinner.description: Roast duck with cabbage and dumplings — the Sunday and holiday centerpiece. The rendered duck fat is saved for cooking.

snacks.name: Chlebíčky (Open-Faced Sandwiches)
ingredients: Toppings: Prague ham, salami, hard-boiled egg, cheese, cucumber, tomato, olive, parsley
instructions: Spread each bread slice with potato salad
Arrange decorative toppings
Garnish with parsley
Arrange on a platter
snacks.description: Czech open-faced sandwiches — found in every deli. Beautifully arranged for parties and afternoon snacks.

snacks.name: Utopenci (Drowned Sausages)
instructions: Slice sausages lengthwise
Layer in jar with onion rings, spices
Mix vinegar, oil, sugar, salt into brine
Pour over sausages
Seal, refrigerate at least 3 days
Serve cold with bread and beer
snacks.description: Pickled sausages — 'drowned men' in vinegar and onions. The classic Czech beer snack, found in every pub.

snacks.name: Trdelník (Chimney Cake)
ingredients: Dough: 500g flour, 7g yeast, 250ml warm milk, 60g sugar, 60g butter, 2 egg yolks, salt
Optional fillings: ice cream, Nutella, whipped cream
instructions: Make sweet yeast dough, let rise 1 hour
Roll dough into long strips
Wrap strips around a wooden or metal cylinder (trdelník roller)
Roll the wrapped cylinder in sugar-walnut-cinnamon mix
Bake over heat (traditionally charcoal, or in oven at 200°C) rotating until golden and caramelized
Slide off the cylinder — the hollow center is for filling
The caramelized sugar shell should be crispy and slightly charred
Fill with ice cream, Nutella, or eat plain
Prague tourists have made this the most photographed pastry in Europe — locals debate whether it's actually traditional
snacks.description: The chimney cake that took over Prague's tourist streets — dough wrapped around a cylinder, rolled in cinnamon-walnut-sugar, baked until caramelized. The hollow center gets stuffed with ice cream for Instagram. The most viral pastry debate in food tourism: tourists love it, some Czechs say it's actually Hungarian/Slovak.

desserts.name: Trdelník (Chimney Cake)
ingredients: Dough: 500g flour, 200ml warm milk, 7g yeast, 2 eggs, 80g sugar, 80g butter, salt
instructions: Make enriched yeast dough, rise 1 hour
Roll into long strips
Wrap strips around a wooden cylinder, spiraling
Brush with butter
Roast over coals or bake at 200°C, rotating, until golden
Roll in cinnamon-sugar-walnut mixture while hot
desserts.description: Spiral pastry baked on a cylinder — crispy, sugary, warm from the oven. Found at every Christmas market in Prague.

desserts.name: Koláče (Czech Kolaches)
ingredients: Dough: 500g flour, 200ml milk, 7g yeast, 2 eggs, 100g sugar, 100g butter
Fillings: plum jam (povidla), sweet cottage cheese (tvaroh), poppy seed paste
instructions: Make enriched dough, rise 1 hour
Shape rounds, press indentation in center
Fill with plum jam, tvaroh, or poppy seed paste
Top with crumble
Rise 20 min
Bake at 190°C for 15-18 min
desserts.description: Round filled pastries — the Czech koláč. The three-filling plate (tvaroh, poppy, plum) is traditional.

drinks.name: Czech Pilsner (Pivo)
instructions: The beer must be draft (čepované)
Pour slowly at an angle, creating a thick foam head
The foam should be 2-3 fingers thick — it protects the beer
Drink slowly
drinks.description: The Czechs drink more beer per capita than any nation on Earth. Pilsner was invented in Plzeň in 1842.

drinks.name: Becherovka and Tonic (BeTon)
instructions: Fill glass with ice
Pour Becherovka
Top with tonic water
Garnish with lemon
drinks.description: Becherovka — Karlovy Vary's secret herbal liqueur since 1807. Mixed with tonic it's nicknamed BeTon (Czech for concrete).
